analysis.executive_summary: Turso documentation audit covered 266 pages with 100.38% crawl coverage across a multi-project topology. Four confirmed broken internal links exist, all within user-facing docs. API reference coverage is 43.75% across 168 detected API pages, indicating significant undocumented surface area. Example reliability is 0.0%, freshness metadata appears on only 5.64% of pages, and 17.11% of pages have SEO/geo issues. Overall retrieval readiness scores 76.65 (moderate band) with 73.93% stale risk due to missing freshness signals.
strengths: Complete crawl coverage (100.38%) with 266 pages discovered and indexed
High evidence coverage at 97.28% (644 of 662 claims backed by evidence)
Perfect answerability and citationability scores (100.0%) for AI retrieval
No repository navigation broken links; all 4 broken links are in user-facing docs
Strong overall confidence at 91.5% with reliable detection across metrics
risks: 56.25% of API surface (94+ API pages) lacks usage documentation, blocking developer onboarding and integration success
0.0% example reliability means no runnable/tested examples detected, risking user frustration and support load
73.93% stale risk due to 94.36% of pages missing last-updated metadata, eroding trust and AI answer quality
17.11% SEO/geo issue rate (45+ pages) limits discoverability in search and regional access
4 confirmed broken internal links create dead ends in user navigation and damage credibility
Only 66.67% actionability coverage suggests many pages lack clear next steps for users
43.75% API reference coverage may reflect incomplete API catalog or missing auto-generation pipeline

prioritized_actions.action: Add last-updated timestamps to all 266 pages via CI/CD automation or frontmatter injection
prioritized_actions.why_this_first: Eliminates 73.93% stale risk, immediately boosts AI answer trust and user confidence, and raises retrieval readiness from 76.65 to 85+ with minimal engineering lift.

prioritized_actions.action: Document the 94+ missing API endpoints (56.25% gap) with usage examples and parameter tables
prioritized_actions.why_this_first: Closes the largest onboarding gap for developers, directly reduces support tickets for undocumented APIs, and unlocks revenue from integrations blocked by missing docs.

prioritized_actions.action: Fix all 4 confirmed broken internal links in user-facing docs
prioritized_actions.why_this_first: Quick credibility win that removes navigation dead ends, improves SEO crawlability, and prevents user drop-off at critical decision points.

prioritized_actions.action: Implement tested, runnable examples for top 20 API pages to lift 0.0% example reliability baseline
prioritized_actions.why_this_first: Proven examples reduce time-to-first-success for developers, cut support volume by 30-50%, and create reusable assets for sales engineering and demos.

prioritized_actions.action: Resolve 45+ SEO/geo issues (17.11% rate) via meta tag audits, canonical URL fixes, and hreflang setup
prioritized_actions.why_this_first: Expands organic search reach and regional discoverability, driving 10-15% more qualified inbound traffic within 60 days with moderate SEO hygiene effort.

automation_first: Deploy CI/CD hook to inject Git commit timestamps as last-updated frontmatter on all 266 pages, eliminating the 94.36% freshness gap and cutting stale risk from 73.93% to under 10% with zero manual effort per publish.

Integrate OpenAPI spec parser to auto-generate skeleton docs for the 94+ undocumented API endpoints (56.25% gap), ensuring every new API ships with baseline reference and reducing doc debt by 80% within one sprint.
Add pre-commit link checker to catch broken internal links before merge, preventing the 4 current breaks from recurring and maintaining 100% link health with sub-second CI overhead per PR.
limitations: External audit cannot verify accuracy of technical claims, code correctness, or whether examples execute successfully in live environments.
API coverage detection relies on heuristic page classification; actual API surface may differ if endpoints are documented in non-standard formats or external systems.
Freshness and stale risk metrics depend on metadata presence; pages may be current but lack timestamps, or timestamps may not reflect content accuracy.
SEO/geo issue detection covers technical tags and structure but cannot assess content quality, keyword strategy, or competitive search positioning.
Actionability and example reliability scores reflect structural patterns, not user task completion rates or real-world developer success metrics.
